head_commit.message:
Construct the interleaving instead of hoping for it: the host was deciding

Two shapes of `test_the_atomic_update_predicate_does_not_prevent_running_but_deleted` have now
failed in CI, and between them they say what the real problem was.

  1. A single `race` asserting one outcome failed on the first run the `database-tests` job
     ever got: `{'B': 'COMMITTED', 'A': 'RuntimeError:None'}` -- session A refusing at
     `rowcount == 0`. That is the OTHER interleaving, not a contradiction of the finding.
  2. Repeating it up to 20 times and asserting only that the bad interleaving is REACHABLE
     passed on one runner, on its first attempt, and then failed on the next run with
     "session A refused at rowcount == 0 in 20 of them".

Twenty for twenty, having previously reproduced immediately. So the interleaving is decided by
the HOST, not by chance -- bimodal per runner, not random within a runner. Repetition cannot
fix that and a larger count cannot either, which is exactly what shape 2's own failure message
said to conclude rather than raising it.

`mid` releases both sessions together and then nothing orders them, and the runner commits
each session only when its body returns. So two new bodies rendezvous twice more, through two
`threading.Event`s the test hangs on the world object:

    B: INSERT the deployment, do not commit    -> w.inserted.set()
    A: UPDATE ... NOT EXISTS, record rowcount  -> w.updated.set()
    B: return, and only now does the runner commit

Under READ COMMITTED A's subquery cannot see B's uncommitted row, `NOT EXISTS` holds,
`rowcount` is 1, both commit, and the terminal state is archived + live. A cannot block on B
either: B's uncommitted INSERT is in `strategy_deployments`, MVCC does not block readers of
it, and A's UPDATE targets `strategies`, which B never touches.

NEW BODIES RATHER THAN EDITED ONES, DELIBERATELY. `_deploy_body` is run by BOTH sessions in
`test_two_real_sessions_both_land_a_live_deployment`; adding a wait to it would deadlock that
test. `race` is untouched -- the Events ride on the world object it already passes to every
body, so no signature changes and no other test is affected.

THE CLAIM IS NARROWER NOW, AND SAYS SO. It is that the atomic NOT EXISTS predicate does not
prevent running-but-deleted WHEN THE WRITES INTERLEAVE THIS WAY. It says nothing about how
often that interleaving occurs in production, which is a question about load rather than
correctness -- and "sometimes" is all a race needs to be worth closing. The assertion message
records what it would mean if this ever passes: the database-level half of clause 1.16 is
closed and the application-level Requirement 2.16 guard should be revisited.

Verified as far as is possible here: flake8 E9,F63,F7,F82 reports 0; the file collects and its
two source-level tests pass (2 passed, 7 skipped -- the seven are `@requires_postgres` and
there is no local server). The constructed interleaving itself is exercised in CI.

head_commit.message:
Unblock the PR gate, and fix the defects it was hiding

THE GATE HAD NEVER PASSED. `gh run list --workflow 01-pr-check.yml` returns five runs
and five failures, oldest 2026-08-29. `gh run view` on the most recent shows
`validate-code` passing the import audit, the dependency audit and flake8, then dying at
`Black Format Check` -- and `Unit & Integration Tests`, `Database Tests (PostgreSQL)` and
`Docker Build Validation` absent from the job list entirely, because all three declare
`needs: validate-code`.

So the 12,000-test backend suite has never executed in CI, nor the PostgreSQL lane task
13.21 built, nor the Docker validation. Measured locally: black would reformat 350 of 382
files under `backend_app/` and isort disagrees with 142, against a tree with no
`pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `.isort.cfg` or `tox.ini` anywhere -- both tools run on
pure defaults against a codebase never formatted with them.

`validate-code` is split. `static-audit` keeps the import audit, dependency audit and
flake8 (correctness checks; flake8 reports 0) and is what the test jobs now depend on.
`format-check` runs black and isort with `continue-on-error`, pinned, reporting the
backlog instead of blocking on it. The display name `Code Quality & Static Audit` is
unchanged so branch-protection required checks still match. NOT fixed by reformatting:
350 files in one commit would conflict with every branch in flight, and isort would
reorder imports in 142 more in a codebase where import order has side effects
(`ml_models.py` probes tensorflow at import; `rate_limit.py` raises at import without
REDIS_URL). `unit-tests` also had no `timeout-minutes`, harmless only while it never ran
-- set to 90 against task 13.13's measured 52-minute suite, so a hung test cannot burn
GitHub's 360-minute default per pull request.

P0-05: THE ORDER'S EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT NOW TRAVELS WITH IT.
`ExecutionEngine.execute_with_idempotency` opens with `assert_live_environment`, and no
caller anywhere passed it an environment, so the `ExecutionEnvironment.LIVE` default won
on every call and the one branch that can refuse was unreachable. A paper bot's order was
processed by the live funnel, passed the live-only assertion, and recorded with an audit
trail that said LIVE. `BotRunner._inner_loop` now passes
`PAPER if self.paper_trading else LIVE`, and `ExecutionEngine.execute_trade` -- a second,
thinner door with five production callers -- forwards `self.execution_environment` instead
of dropping it.

AND THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH WAS A LAUNCH BLOCKER. `routers/strategies.py` starts bots with
`paper_trading=True` hardcoded at both deploy sites, so paper is the ordinary path;
labelling those orders truthfully had every one of them refused, swallowed by the tick
loop's `except Exception` into an error per signal. Resolved by distinguishing the live
order path from a declared simulator rather than by removing the label. Requirement 13.9
governs the path that can "issue an exchange call", and an engine stating PAPER/BACKTEST
with no `exchange_executor` cannot: it gets `assert_simulation_environment_matches`, where
13.10 still applies in full, LIVE is refused (which the live-path guard could not do for
it), and only its own environment is admitted. Every other engine -- holding an executor,
stating LIVE, or stating nothing (65 of 71 construction sites) -- keeps
`assert_live_environment` unchanged. The full (engine, executor, order) matrix is
enumerated in tests/test_simulated_orders_reach_the_simulator.py; three rows got stricter,
and the two combinations that can reach `place_order` are asserted by measuring whether
`place_order` was called, not inferred.

TWO TEST-POLLUTION CLASSES, EACH WORTH ~20 FAILURES.
`_op_deploy` in tests/test_strategy_lifecycle_concurrency.py wrapped its work in
`with patch(...)` on three module globals while being driven by `asyncio.gather` -- twice
concurrently in one test. Interleaved entries unwind so that the last exit writes a MOCK
back as the module global, permanently: every later test in the session then resolved
every caller's plan as `free`, and tests/test_training_worker.py lost 20+ tests to
`CAP_EXCEEDED (MAX_EPOCHS: requested 4 rounds, allowed 0 rounds)`. Confirmed by running
the two files together and confirmed PRE-EXISTING by re-running with the change stashed.
Hoisted into one autouse fixture per test; the patched values are constants, so the four
operations still race exactly as the two xfail P0 proofs require. 20+ failures ->
104 passed, 2 xfailed.

In the frontend, tests/unit/pages/strategyMarketplace.test.jsx mocked `../../../src/api`
with only `default: { library }`. A `vi.mock` factory replaces the whole module, so the
omitted `isAuthenticated` -- which `useEntitlements.load()` opens with -- threw on every
render, as 57 UNHANDLED REJECTIONS. Every test passed while the hook was broken, and
Vitest 4 exits non-zero on unhandled errors, so `npx vitest --run` failed the job with
nothing reported as failing. Stubbed to `false`, the behaviour-preserving choice: the
anonymous branch makes no request, which is the state these tests were already in by
throwing. 57 -> 0, exit 0.

REQUIREMENT 2.16 IS A PROVEN P0, NOW PINNED RATHER THAN BROADCAST.
start/stop/delete/deploy raced against one strategy lands running-but-deleted in 21 of 40
seeded interleavings and double-deploy in 12 of 12; there is no asyncio.Lock, no
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and no version guard on any of the four write paths. Both tests were
written to fail deliberately, which was sound while nothing ran them -- in a lane that
gates merges, a deliberately-failing test is indistinguishable from a regression. Marked
xfail(strict=True) with the diagnosis, so they XPASS and fail the build the day a guard
lands. Not fixed here: the double-deploy half already has a database guard
(021_strategy_deployment_live_uniqueness.sql, proven in the database-tests job), and
closing running-but-deleted needs a PostgreSQL-verified migration, which this change
cannot test.

STALE TESTS CORRECTED AGAINST DELIBERATE CHANGES, NOT RELAXED.
tests/test_ws_ticket_redemption.py asserted the `?token=` overlap release that commit
c60546c6 ended (session JWTs were being recorded by every access log); the assertion is
inverted to pin the removal. tests/test_my_strategies_ownership_and_actions.py listed six
`strategies` columns as unprovable that 020_declare_pre_existing_tables.sql now declares;
its escape-hatch map is emptied as its own error message instructed, and its
root-directory proof moved to a column 020 does not declare. tests/test_billing_e2e.py
greps Billing.jsx for literals that Requirement 3.1's sentence case and task 8.1's shared
socket client changed -- and `test_billing_jsx_has_cancel_button` was PASSING on the
400-line header comment that quotes the old title-cased label, so these now strip comments
before asserting.

tests/regression/baseline/surface_strategies.json is re-recorded additively (19 lines
added, 0 removed) for the two refusals this change adds to POST /deploy --
DEPLOY_PARAMETER_NOT_APPLICABLE (422) and DEPLOY_BLUEPRINT_INCOMPLETE (409) -- using the
`_baseline_note_raises` mechanism the regression suite defines for an authorised
re-record, following the precedent in auth_token.json and billing_entitlements.json.

Also in this change: the distributed-execution paths that claimed an exchange and
simulated. All three are unreachable (`submit_order_idempotent` has no callers; the
gateway needs a WorkerPool only `ExecutionOrchestrator.initialize()` creates and nothing
calls it, so POST /api/distributed-execution/submit-job is a 400 on every request), which
is what makes stating LIVE safe -- it turns a latent trap into a refusal with no live path
to break. `ExchangeGateway.execute_order` stops substituting an `order_{hex}` id and a
`Decimal("50000")` fill price for values it does not have, and
`ExecutionWorker._complete_job_with_result` stops recording a refusal as a COMPLETED job
with zeroed figures and emitting `on_order_execution` for it.

VERIFICATION. 809 tests green across the files touched (597 across ws-ticket,
my-strategies, billing, lifecycle, regression, training worker/status/endpoints, exchange
safety and deploy gates; 212 across the execution-environment and paper/live set). flake8
E9/F63/F7/F82 reports 0 and the import audit reports PASS. Frontend measured in bounded
chunks: 155 files, 3,702 passed, 0 real failures.

NOT VERIFIED, AND FLAGGED AS SUCH: the registryClient partial mock in
tests/unit/builder/enginePaths.test.jsx. It stops the only test that mounts
`DataPipelineProvider` from making a real axios GET to the registry timeframes endpoint,
which jsdom reports as an `AggregateError` and Vitest 4 turns into a non-zero exit with
every test passing. The host ran out of memory and disk before a passing run could be
taken. It is a test-only change and cannot affect production behaviour; the first CI run
proves or disproves it.

The full 12,000-test lane has still never run anywhere. It is expected to surface more.

head_commit.message:
Stop writing session JWTs to CloudWatch: the ?token= socket credential is deleted

Uvicorn's access log writes the full WebSocket request line including the
query string, so every handshake on the legacy ?token= arm put a live
session JWT into /ecs/vyomquant-api beside the user id and the client IP.

Task 8.2 kept that arm for one release and wrote down the condition for
removing it. The condition is now measured as met: per-UTC-day token/ticket
handshake counts are 09-27 24/6, 09-28 39/12, 09-29 3/89, 09-30 0/0,
10-01 12/2, 10-02 2/136. Tickets dominate 136-to-2 since verify_ws_ticket
was deployed.

Server: the token query parameter is removed from all nine @ws_router
routes, and the token branch and parameter from both _resolve_ws_credential
and _resolve_ws_subject. The four 'if not ticket and not token' guards
become 'if not ticket', which narrows what is admitted. Route count is
unchanged at 351.

Client: the WS_TICKET_FALLBACK deploy-ordering shim is deleted. With the
server arm gone it could only produce a socket the server refuses, turning
a clean 4001 into a retry loop re-presenting an unredeemable credential.
The ~2/day sticky sessions get one 4001 and then recover on their own,
because _open mints a fresh ticket on every attempt and scheduleReconnect
re-enters it via connectPath rather than reusing the spent URL.

/ws/strategy is refused rather than migrated: its ownership read ran under
the user's JWT so strategies RLS enforced it, and a ticket carries only a
subject. Dropping to an unscoped read would swap that control for a weaker
one, so it is left as a decision. No client in src/ connects there; the
live equivalent is the strategy.{id} channel subscription.

Guards: a new AST guard asserts no route signature or body takes token and
neither resolver has a token branch, with _validate_ws_token exempted by
name. The existing fail-closed suite is extended to prove 4001 on all nine
routes with no credential, and that a valid JWT as ?token= is now refused
on all nine - 8 of 9 admitted it before this change.

Requirements: 1.21 (PARTIAL - /ws/strategy named), 2.21, 3.9

head_commit.message:
Retoken the last off-palette hues, and take four colour-ratchet entries to zero

NOTE ON PROVENANCE: this is a parallel session's work, committed from a shared working tree
on the repository owner's instruction. The description below is read off the diff and off
the ratchet entries the diff rewrites, not from that session's intent. The verification is
mine.

WHAT THE DIFF DOES

Five files were still drawing hand-mixed hues that no token backs, and the ratchet in
tests/unit/guards/no-colour-literals.budget.js recorded each as an accepted debt rather than
a violation. Those entries go 18 / 30 / 3 / 37 / 1 -> 0, and the budget file keeps the
entries at 0 rather than deleting them, so a literal cannot come back unnoticed.

  components/SupportCenter.jsx (37)  The last whole page carrying a palette of its own, and
  the interesting part is WHY the existing guards did not see it: an earlier task replaced
  the `const C = { ... }` this page declared, which is what no-local-tokens.test.js watches,
  but the seven hues in STATUS_CONFIG and PRIORITY_CONFIG were never in that object. A guard
  that watches declaration sites cannot see a palette inlined into two frozen maps. None of
  the seven was in tokens.css, so an OPEN chip at /app/support drew a different red, and a
  RESOLVED chip a different green, from every ds/StatusBadge elsewhere. Labels, icons and the
  { bg, text } shape are untouched, so no call site moved.

  components/DeployPreflightPanel.jsx (30)  The largest off-palette set left in the tree, and
  not one of its four verdict hues was in the palette - they were Tailwind's emerald, red,
  yellow and slate ramps. The panel renders inside the deploy modal, so a FAILED row drew a
  different red from the ds/StatusBadge reading FAILED in the table the modal had opened over.
  The four presentations now come from design/semantic.js by state word. The border STYLE is
  untouched: solid for verdicts, dashed for pending and unreadable, because that axis carries
  meaning independently of colour.

  components/common/primitives.jsx (18)  Tag2's tones move onto the group each already meant:
  profit/loss to status.profit/status.loss (a profit tag no longer draws #26A69A text inside
  an #00C853 border), warning and gold collapse onto the one declared amber, purple becomes
  status.neutral - the palette holds no purple and that tone's text was already neutral.
  Toast's hand-tuned elevation becomes shadow.raised. The base border keeps 0.30 and the
  hover 0.15, written off the group's own fg, because the brightening between them is the
  chip's only hover feedback.

  components/FirstTradeWizard.jsx (3) and NotificationCenter.jsx (1)  Pure white and pure
  black on brand fills, where the palette declares #F0F2F5 and #080A0E.

Two off-palette constructs went with them that the ratchet is structurally blind to, because
they carry no literal: `hover:border-cyan-500/40` on ui/Card.jsx and the same utility on
StrategyDetail.jsx's backtest and signal cards - Tailwind's own cyan ramp (#06B6D4), not the
brand (#00D4FF), on every hoverable card in the application. ui/Button.jsx's secondary
variant had carried the identical mistake, which makes a default-ramp utility the most common
thing a hex-literal guard cannot catch. StrategyDetail's executions table also moves a 5%
pure-white row hover onto surface-raised, which is ds/DataTable's own interactive-row hover.

Also: components/admin/AdminDashboard.jsx, same class of substitution.

Two states now share an amber in SupportCenter, and the budget file records that rather than
hiding it: the palette carries four content-bearing hues for six ticket states, so
in_progress and waiting_for_support land together. Both were yellow-orange at 12% in a 9px
chip and both carried the same Clock icon, and each state still states its own word. The
alternative - inventing a sixth hue - is the one thing a consistency pass must not do.

VERIFICATION (mine, on the combined tree)

eslint 0 errors (135 warnings, unchanged). vite build green. Full frontend suite 3707 of
3712 passing. The four failing files are the documented order-dependent flake family, not
this change: dashboard_phase2a_ui and backtestStrategySelection pass in isolation, and
dashboard-alert-strip and builder/enginePaths fail alone but pass together, 34/34 - they are
timing-dependent on an unhandled jsdom XHR, which is why they move between runs.

NOT VERIFIED: that this is the complete intended change, and no visual review was performed.
Several substitutions change what is drawn on purpose - a 12% #F59E0B is not a 10% #FFAB00 -
so the chips in SupportCenter, DeployPreflightPanel and Tag2 look different now, which is the
point of the pass but is worth seeing before it reaches users.

head_commit.message:
Close the three findings left open after the billing work: a risk swallow, an unaskable question, and a dead socket layer

1. routers/risk.py answered a database failure with an empty allowance list
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
GET /api/risk/strategy-limits caught a failed strategy_limits read, logged it at DEBUG, and
answered 200 with whatever the in-memory map held - on a fresh process
{"limits": [], "count": 0}. An empty list and an unreadable list are different facts and they
render identically: RiskSettings.jsx titles the panel "Strategy capital allocations (0)" and
shows nothing, which reads as "no per-strategy limits are configured". A trader who concludes
that may size a position as though no cap applies, while the cap sits in a table the endpoint
could not reach and paper_trading_service goes on enforcing it.

It now raises 503 STRATEGY_LIMITS_FETCH_FAILED and logs at error. Partial is deliberately not
offered: returning the in-memory subset labelled as the whole list is the same lie in a smaller
font. The success contract is untouched - limits, count and user_id keep their names, types and
meaning - so no client that reads them is affected; what changed is that the failure path is
reachable and named instead of disguised as a successful empty read.

Scoped on purpose. `sb is None` (no token, or create_request_supabase_async refused) still falls
through to the in-memory store, and GET /api/risk/settings has the identical shape over a
defaulted record - answering 200 with max_daily_loss 500.0, a figure nothing on that path
measured. Closing either means redefining what a None from the module-shared _sb means for every
handler in the file, since it conflates "no token" with "construction failed". Both are recorded
in docs/pre-existing-test-failures.md rather than half-fixed here.

One test changed with it, and it was passing THROUGH the defect.
test_risk_management_lifecycle.py::test_strategy_limits_crud reached a real
create_request_supabase_async, got a client, and its GET failed the read with getaddrinfo failed -
which the handler swallowed into a 200 carrying only the in-memory record. Its assertions
appeared to verify that the read works and actually verified that a failed read was ignored. It
now pins _sb to None, the honest description of an environment with no persisted store, where the
in-memory record IS the whole answer and count == 1 is a true claim about it.
test_risk_settings_api.py already patched _sb for the same reason.

2. "Is migration 017 applied?" was a question the tooling could not ask
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Nothing in this repository applies backend_app/migrations/*.sql automatically, and the
application is written to DEGRADE when 017's objects are absent: _PROFILE_COLUMN_SETS retries
without plan_limit_overrides, the billing entitlements read drops to the pre-017 column set, and
collect_usage reports the metered figures as unavailable instead of inventing zeros. That
tolerance is correct - it stops a deploy landing before a migration from 500-ing every gated
route - and it is exactly why an unapplied 017 is INVISIBLE: the product works, the billing cycle
silently never renders, and the durable usage ledger silently does not exist. A degradation nobody
can observe is one nobody fixes.

scripts/migration_preflight.py already knows how to answer this; it just stopped at 014. It now
carries CHECK_ONLY_MIGRATION_IDS (015-018), ALL_CHECKABLE_MIGRATION_FILES, and a read-only --all
flag.

A SECOND list rather than a longer MIGRATION_IDS, which is the whole point:
apply_migrations.py imports MIGRATION_FILES and uses it directly as its files_to_run, so
appending would not have widened a checker - it would have widened what an --apply run EXECUTES
against a production database. tests/test_migration_tooling.py already pinned the two lists to
each other and that pin was doing its job. Eight new tests hold the line: the ranges are
disjoint, the applier's set is unchanged, 017's parsed expectations really contain both profiles
columns, the ledger columns, the unique constraint, the index and the RLS flag, 016 reports
NO-CHECKABLE-OBJECTS rather than passing vacuously, --all widens what is probed, and --all issues
nothing but SELECTs. The parser needed no addition.

I could not run it against production: the local .env carries SUPABASE_URL=dummy.url, so there
are no credentials here to probe with. The command is documented in
docs/PRICING_AND_ENTITLEMENTS.md and answers APPLIED / NOT-APPLIED / PARTIAL with the missing
objects named.

3. The WebSocket layer is dead, and CloudFront is the one refusing it
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Every authenticated page shows CONNECTION FAILED and "Not connected to the trading engine" while
the REST API, the catalogue and the whole SPA work. Same host, same path, one header different:

    GET /ws/telemetry                        -> 404, server: uvicorn, JSON body   (origin answered)
    GET /ws/telemetry + Upgrade: websocket   -> 403, no server header, length 0   (CDN answered)

So /ws/* IS routed to the ALB; the moment the request carries the upgrade, CloudFront answers it
itself without consulting the origin. True of both the custom domain and
d7d88qs4jmch.cloudfront.net. Cause: scripts/add_ws_behavior_cloudfront.py created the /ws/*
behaviour by CLONING /api/*, which carried over a cache configuration that strips Upgrade and
Connection. The path pattern is right; the header policy is not.

Ruled out along the way, each with evidence: routing (the 404 above), a token-store mismatch
(apiClient.js and websocketClient.js both read sessionStorage "token"), the ticket endpoint
(POST /api/auth/ws-ticket answers 401 unauthenticated, correctly), and the WS_TICKET_FALLBACK
deploy-ordering shim (it switches to the legacy ?token= credential on a 4001/1006 refusal, which
never arrives because the refusal is not the application's).

The remedy is an origin request policy that forwards the handshake headers plus a non-caching
policy on that behaviour. That is infrastructure, not code, so it is NOT applied here - it is
written up with the exact remediation and the one-line reproduction in
docs/websocket-upgrade-at-the-edge.md.

What IS applied is the gate that would have caught it. 06-frontend-deploy.yml ran thirteen steps
and never exercised the deployed application: the build-time check greps the bundle for an
allowed API hostname, and d7d88qs4jmch.cloudfront.net is ON that allow-list by design, so a
hostname check could not have caught this and a stale secret passes it too. The new final step
extracts the WS base from the bundle that was just deployed, attempts a real upgrade, and passes
only if the response carries server: uvicorn (or 101). It runs after the S3 sync, so a failure
reports a broken realtime layer rather than rolling the frontend back, and it is blocking because
a trading terminal that cannot open a socket is a product-down condition that has already shipped
silently once.

The gate was tested rather than assumed, and testing it found a defect in the gate: curl drops
Connection: Upgrade when it negotiates HTTP/2, because HTTP/2 forbids that header - so the probe
degraded to a plain GET, the origin answered it, and the step concluded the upgrade had worked.

head_commit.message:
Tell an unreadable subscription apart from a broken endpoint, and make the support reference correlate

A live billing page reported "Could not check your plan - your entitlements are
unreadable, so none are assumed" with the reference req_05bdc1c7-3bc5-4b27-9d75-6dfc97aea291.
Reproduced through the real endpoint: GET /api/billing/entitlements answers
BILLING_ENTITLEMENTS_FAILED in exactly two situations, and only when ENV=production -
the request-scoped profiles read RAISES, or there is no database client. A profiles read
that returns NO ROW answers 200 with plan=free, and outside production the same failure
also answers 200 with free.

So the screenshot was not a defect. It was get_plan_context failing CLOSED exactly as
specified: when it cannot read the subscription it refuses rather than assuming Free,
because assuming Free silently strips a paying account of the capacity it bought. The
service was healthy throughout - /health reported redis, questdb, supabase and fleet all
connected, /api/billing/plans answered 200, and the route returned a correct 401
unauthenticated.

What was wrong is that the refusal was INDISTINGUISHABLE from a defect, in three ways,
none of which is visible from inside the entitlement layer because all three are
properties of the response.

ONE. It was raised as a bare RuntimeError and fell into the handler's catch-all, so a
transient read failure and a genuine bug in the handler produced the same status and the
same error code. The trader could not tell "wait and retry" from "report this", and
neither could whoever picked up the report. It now has its own exception,
subscription_dependencies.PlanVerificationUnavailable, and its own answer: 503
BILLING_PLAN_UNVERIFIABLE with Retry-After. 503 rather than 500 because nothing in the
handler is wrong - an upstream read was unavailable, the condition is transient, and the
status is what makes the client's own retry classification truthful.
PlanVerificationUnavailable subclasses RuntimeError deliberately: routers/strategy_operations.py
and backend/model_versioning.py already wrap that call in broad handlers and
tests/test_pricing_ladder.py asserts pytest.raises(RuntimeError) on the fail-closed path,
so all three keep working unchanged while a caller that wants to distinguish the two now
can.

TWO. The support reference on screen matched nothing on the server, and the cause was not
the billing handler. apiClient mints req_<uuid4> per request, sends it as X-Request-ID and
prints it as the support reference - but CorrelationIdMiddleware was registered with its
DEFAULT validator, is_valid_uuid4, which REJECTS that value because the req_ prefix is not
a UUID. The middleware logged "Generated new request ID (...), since request header value
failed validation", replaced it, and every log record and every structured error body for
that request then carried the SERVER's id while the browser showed its own. That applied
to every endpoint in the application, not to billing, which is why the fix is at the
middleware: main.py now supplies a validator that accepts the format this client produces
and a bare uuid4, so curl, the mobile client and an upstream proxy that already sets a
correlation id all keep working. It stays a strict pattern rather than "accept anything",
because an unvalidated inbound header is a log-injection seam - a caller could otherwise
write forged text or a second line into the record identifying its own request. That is
the reason the default validator exists and the reason this one is a regex.

THREE. The handler logged no correlation id at all, so even a correct one would not have
been greppable. Both error arms now log the resolved id and report it in the body, through
a _correlation_id helper that delegates to marketplace.errors.current_request_id - the
platform's existing implementation - so a reference quoted from a billing error and one
quoted from a marketplace error are the same kind of thing. The X-Request-ID RESPONSE
header is left to the middleware, which already sets it; the handler setting it too
appended a second value and the client read back "id, id".

The refusal copy is new on the frontend because the sentence matters here:
BILLING_PLAN_UNVERIFIABLE says the plan could not be read and states plainly that nothing
about the subscription has changed. "No entitlement assumed" on a billing page is easily
read as "my plan was taken away", and a trader who reads it that way opens a billing
ticket about a database hiccup.

tests/test_billing_entitlements_endpoint.py, 27 tests, drives the endpoint over HTTP. That
is the point of it: every service-level assertion over the entitlement layer passed while
this was live, because the fault was in the seam between a correct service and a correct
client - the same gap closed for GET /api/billing/plans in the previous commit. It pins all
four outcomes (readable profile, no row, read raises, no client), the fail-open half
outside production, that the refusal names no driver code or table name, that the
correlation id is echoed on both arms and issued when the client sends none, and the
middleware validator directly - including the log-injection cases, which cannot be proved
through a request because a rejected id and a generated one are the same observation.

Baselines billing_entitlements.json and surface_billing.json re-recorded, additively: one
raise added and request_id added to both details, with _baseline_note_* provenance on each
file. The re-record dropped surface_billing's existing _baseline_note_plan_ladder, which is
restored verbatim.

Verification: new suite 27 passed; regression baselines + the new suite 87 passed; pricing
ladder, entitlement matrix/resolver, billing localization, saas gating audit, route
contract, marketplace error surface, log redaction, rate-limit keys and cover-reference
SSRF 1049 passed; model versioning, ML training governance and profile cache 214 passed.
Frontend design/errorCopy suites 66 passed; eslint 0 errors; vite build green.
test_billing_e2e.py's two JSX-copy failures and
test_exception_swallow_regression.py::test_db_error_returns_503_not_empty_limits are
pre-existing and recorded in docs/pre-existing-test-failures.md - the third is added to
that record here, with the evidence that routers/risk.py is untouched by this work and
imports nothing from the entitlement layer. The frontend full run shows 3681 of 3685
passing, the four being the known Dashboard/StrategyDetail cross-file flake; three pass in
isolation, and the fourth fails WORSE with this commit's only frontend change reverted, so
it is not attributable here.

head_commit.message:
Publish the price list once, in rupees, and show it in the visitor's currency

The landing page quoted the right prices and never localised them; the billing page
localised and quoted the wrong ones. Both symptoms came from one cause: the catalogue
published TWO independent base price columns, INR (0/499/999/2499) and USD
(0/5/10/25), with nothing reconciling them - at the prevailing rate 499 is about $5.20,
so the two columns were different value points roughly 4% apart - and every currency the
catalogue did not publish was converted from the DOLLAR one. So the marketing page
advertised the rupee value point while every non-Indian visitor was quoted the dollar
one, and the landing page hardcoded its figures precisely because the endpoint disagreed
with them.

subscription_engine.PRICE_BASE_CURRENCY = "INR" makes the rupee list the single published
price. Every plan's pricing and pricing_annual now carries one key; the USD column is
deleted rather than reconciled, because a second published column is a second price list
and a second price list drifts. FXService gains major_units, to_usd and convert_major, and
localize_plan_price takes (published_minor, target_currency, base_currency) instead of a
USD base amount: a currency present in the published list is still charged verbatim and
flagged price_source="published", everything else is a conversion of the base flagged
"fx". Publishing a committed USD or EUR price point later is a one-line catalogue change
and is honoured automatically. pricing_service and routers/billing now report base_price
in the base currency with base_currency_symbol beside it, and the ML addon's published
price moved onto the same base.

Verified end to end against the endpoint both price surfaces read, at the recorded
baseline rate of 95.997 INR/USD: 499/999/2499 published; $5.20/$10.41/$26.03,
4.58/9.18/22.96 EUR, 3.92/7.84/19.62 GBP, 19.09/38.22/95.60 AED, 6.64/13.30/33.26 SGD,
818/1637/4095 JPY, all price_source "fx", and the charged amount equal to the shown amount
in every one.

CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: a new USD checkout now converts 499 rather than charging a
flat $5.00, so it moves from $5.00 to about $5.20 and floats with the exchange rate.
Existing subscriptions are unaffected - Stripe amounts are built inline per checkout
session via price_data, so nothing re-prices a live subscription.

components/landing/Pricing.jsx now reads GET /api/billing/plans through a new
api.billing.getPublicPlans and renders plans[].localized_price as sent, with a currency
selector populated from the server's own supported_currencies. getPublicPlans rather than
getPlans because the authenticated transport routes a 401 into the shell's auth:expired
handler, which would turn reading a price list into a sign-out prompt for an anonymous
visitor. The rupee constants survive only as the fallback for a failed read and render
only under the rupee sign; a card waiting on a converted figure shows a placeholder rather
than a rupee number wearing another symbol, the CTA quotes the same figure as the card it
sits on, and the section states whether what is on screen is the published list or a
conversion of it.

Two defects found while testing that layer and fixed here. Choosing a currency used to
leave the previous currency's figures on screen while the read was in flight, with the
selector and the disclosure sentence already showing the new code - $5.20 under a sentence
reading "shown in EUR". The displayed currency is now driven by the response and never by
the pending request, so a figure and its symbol cannot disagree; the selector shows the
pick optimistically only while a read is in flight, and otherwise shows the currency the
figures are actually in. That also handles a currency the server declines to quote - the
selector snaps to the server's answer instead of waiting forever - and a failed re-read,
which keeps the figures it has rather than blanking a correct price. Second, re-choosing
the same currency after a failure was a dead control, because the read was keyed on the
currency alone; it is keyed on an attempt counter too.

components/landing/FAQ.jsx quoted the rupee list verbatim in "How much does it cost to
start?", which became a visible contradiction the moment the cards above it localised. It
now answers the question that was asked - nothing - and points at the pricing section for
the figures. One surface quotes prices and it is the one that cannot be wrong.

tests/test_pricing_ladder.py adds TestThePublicPlansEndpoint, 34 tests driving
GET /api/billing/plans itself across INR, USD, EUR, GBP, JPY and AED. The service-level
assertions above it all passed while the two surfaces disagreed in production, because
the disagreement lived in what the endpoint assembles out of the catalogue. Per currency:
base_price is the published rupee figure and does not move with the display currency, the
quoted figure equals the charged figure, the quote converts back to the published rupee
price within a rounding unit, price_source says which it is, the annual payload is the
server's published figure with its own monthly equivalent, and the custom tier quotes
nothing. 167 passed.

tests/test_billing_localization_e2e.py's server-authority test asserted
pricing["USD"] / 100 == 10.00; it now asserts the published base is the only column and
that a dollar quote is a conversion of 999 rather than a second published figure.
43 passed. The landing regression suite is rewritten for the currency behaviour - 40
tests covering the offline rupee fallback, the localised render, the selector, the
in-flight and failed-read states, zero-decimal currencies, and that getPlans is never
called - and asserts that no published rupee figure appears anywhere on the page while
another currency is on screen, which is what fails the build if a second price list
reappears in the FAQ or anywhere else.

Also corrects three docblocks that asserted base_price was USD (pages/Billing.jsx,
design/pageFields.js) and the pricing section of docs/PRICING_AND_ENTITLEMENTS.md, which
still described the two published columns as intended regional pricing.

Verification: tests/test_pricing_ladder.py 167 passed, test_billing_localization_e2e.py
43 passed, test_route_contract.py + test_pricing_tier_reconciliation.py +
regression/test_baseline_unchanged.py 80 passed, and a billing/entitlement/marketplace
sweep of ten suites 232 passed. test_billing_e2e.py's two JSX-copy failures are
pre-existing and recorded in docs/pre-existing-test-failures.md. Frontend: 3710 of 3712
passing, the two being the known dashboard_phase2d_polish full-run flake that passes in
isolation; eslint 0 errors; vite build green.

head_commit.message:
Add the five-plan VyomQuant pricing ladder and enforce it end to end

Free / Trader / Pro Quant / Business / Enterprise at Rs0 / 499 / 999 / 2,499 /
quoted, with published annual prices of Rs4,990 / 9,990 / 24,990.

ONE CATALOGUE
core/subscription_engine.py is the single authoritative definition: identifiers,
display names, prices, capacity and features. PLAN_LIMITS and PLAN_FEATURES are
derived indexes, not second copies. The frontend reads it over the wire; the one
exception is the public pricing section, whose rupee constants are pinned against
the catalogue by two independent test transcriptions.

`enterprise` IS THE BUSINESS TIER
It was the historic Rs2,499 plan, so the display name moved and the identifier did
not: every existing subscriber lands on Business with no migration and no capacity
loss. Making `enterprise` mean the new custom tier was rejected because
migrate_plan_key resolves live values to themselves, which would have left a stored
`enterprise` permanently ambiguous between a legacy subscriber and a new contract.
The custom tier takes a new id, `scale`.

COUNTED VS METERED
Strategies, deployments, exchange connections, ML models, listings and marketplace
subscriptions are counted from the persistence layer at check time; a maintained
counter drifts from the rows it describes and then either locks a customer out of
capacity they own or hands them capacity they do not. Backtests, optimization runs
and ML training are metered per calendar month, period-scoped in the key, and are
never returned on completion - which is what stops delete-and-retry resetting the
month. plan_usage_ledger is the durable record behind the Redis meter, rebuilt into
it on a cache miss so a flush cannot hand every account a fresh month.

ENFORCEMENT
core/subscription_dependencies.py is the only enforcement path and trusts nothing
from the client. It fails closed: an unreadable profile raises, an unreadable usage
figure answers 503 rather than assuming zero. Refusals are structured 403s carrying
a stable code, the measured current and limit, the required plan, and the server's
own upgrade copy - so the UI renders the verdict instead of restating the ladder.

Gates wired on: create-strategy, clone, deploy, backtest (3 routes), optimization
(4 routes), ML training, exchange connect, marketplace checkout, publish,
submissions and listing settings.

Two gates are functions rather than dependencies because the request body decides
whether a slot is consumed: an exchange key ROTATION adds no connection, and an ML
RETRAIN replaces a model rather than adding one. Both refused legitimate operations
as plain quota checks.

MARKETPLACE
Browsing opens to every plan - /marketplace is public, so the old gate withheld from
a signed-in Free account something a stranger could see. Subscribing starts at
Trader (3/10/25), publishing at Pro Quant (5/15). The 90/10 split runs through the
existing money.split_ninety_ten and settlement_service; no second payment path, and
the catalogue constant is asserted equal to OWNER_SHARE_PERCENT rather than restated.

BILLING
Razorpay and Stripe integrations unchanged. Adds a billing interval (month/year,
defaulting to month so existing clients are unaffected).

Fixes a real pricing defect at the root: PricingService FX-converted the USD base
for every currency, so GET /api/billing/plans answered about Rs865 for the Rs999
plan and Razorpay was asked for that amount. The landing page hardcoded its figures
because the endpoint disagreed with them. FXService.localize_plan_price now charges
the published figure for a currency the catalogue publishes and converts only for
one it does not, reporting which via price_source.

MIGRATION 017, AND WHY DEPLOY ORDER IS NOT LOAD-BEARING
Adds profiles.billing_interval, profiles.plan_limit_overrides and
plan_usage_ledger. Idempotent, no UPDATE against profiles, both columns nullable
with no backfill; Razorpay subscription ids, invoices and settlement history are
untouched.

PostgREST fails a whole statement on an unknown column, so code reaching a database
that has not run the migration would otherwise 500 every gated route (the plan read
fails closed) and, worse, lose the tier on the entitlement write that runs after the
customer has been charged. Both now degrade by column: the plan read retries with
the pre-migration column set, and the tier is written even if the interval cannot be
recorded. Apply the migration anyway - overrides and billing cycle are inert until
it runs.

DOWNGRADE
Deletes nothing. Over-capacity is reported from the server, which holds both the
measured usage and the new limits. No live strategy is terminated and no exchange
connection is invalidated by a plan change.

FRONTEND
New gate layer - FeatureGate, PlanGate, UsageLimit, CapacityNotice, UpgradePrompt,
LockedCommand - over one shared single-flight entitlements read, replacing four
surfaces that called the endpoint independently and could disagree. Gates fail
closed and render the server's copy; an unreadable figure shows the server's reason,
never a fabricated zero. The frontend decides what to show and never what is
allowed.

Landing page: new positioning, three product paths, marketplace discover/subscribe/
deploy, creator section with the 90/10 split, the seven-stage workflow with its plan
boundaries in the diagram, five pricing cards, and a capacity table of figures the
platform actually enforces. No team, workspace, RBAC or API-tier claims, and the
word "unlimited" appears nowhere under #pricing.

Billing page: all thirteen allowances driven by the server's own quotas rather than
four hardcoded tiles, monthly allowances labelled as such, an over-capacity notice,
and a monthly/annual toggle priced from one response.

NOT ENFORCEABLE, AND SAID SO
Custom indicators have no per-account store in this platform, so usage_ledger.count
refuses to answer for them rather than reporting a fabricated zero. Trading accounts
are counted from paper_accounts; no trading_accounts table exists. Enterprise
capacity is a recorded override falling back to the Business figure, not unlimited.

TESTS
New: tests/test_pricing_ladder.py (129 cases, transcribing the published table
independently of the catalogue so the two cannot drift) and a frontend gate suite
(30 cases). Ten existing suites updated to the new contract; five regression
baselines re-recorded with the provenance notes that authorise them.

Also fixes a pre-existing flaky guard: test_marketplace_error_surface scanned the
random 32-char hex request_id for the literal 5432, the Postgres port, and failed on
collision. And adds a conftest fixture clearing the plan cache and monthly meters
between tests, since a reservation that accumulates - correctly - now leaks across
files.

Backend 1213 passed across every affected suite. Frontend 3695/3696 (one
pre-existing full-run flake that passes in isolation), lint clean, build green.
Order execution, the risk engine, exchange credentials, trading workers and
reconciliation are untouched.

head_commit.message:
Create the strategy version a save promises, and stop the ownership list 503ing

Two unrelated production defects, neither in the page that reported them.

THE BACKTESTER REFUSED EVERY SAVED STRATEGY. POST /api/strategies wrote one row, into `strategies`, and tucked the compiled plan inside the `buy_logic` JSONB. It never created a `strategy_versions` row, and no other HTTP route did either: a search for `is_current` finds it in migrations 001/003 and in StrategyService, and no router called any of the service methods that write it. Four readers require that row with `is_current = TRUE` - `get_strategy`'s `owned['version']`, `_load_backtest_version` (the 422 'This strategy has no saved version' the trader saw), `GET /api/strategies/{id}/versions` (the Backtester's `is_current` lookup) and `_assert_deploy_prerequisites` - so a strategy saved, listed, and could be neither backtested nor deployed by any route. The save was the half that was wrong, not the four readers.

The save now persists the version through `StrategyService.create_version`, handed the `CompiledVersion` the request already produced so the compiler runs once. Going through the service rather than inlining an INSERT keeps one writer for the canonical columns (Requirement 9.1), the degrade to the legacy `execution_graph` column when migration 004 is unapplied, the previous `is_current` clear that `check_single_current_version` needs, the `strategies.current_version` repoint, the registry snapshot and the VERSION_CREATED audit record. `_persist_current_version` never raises: it runs after the strategies row is written, so a raise would answer a save that succeeded with a 500 and tell the author their strategy was lost while it sits in their list. The outcome is on the response instead - `version_saved` always, plus a code and a sentence when false, and no `version` key, so the Builder's `serverVersionLabel` finds no label to name rather than naming one that does not exist.

PUT /api/strategies/{id} FAILED EVERY RE-SAVE. It passed the request body straight into `.update(body)`, and `buildSavePayload` sends `graph_json`, `nodes` and `edges` - none of them columns of `strategies`. PostgREST answered 42703/PGRST204 and the route turned that into its 503, so the first save (POST, which folds the graph into `buy_logic`) worked and every save after it did not. A graph-carrying body is now compiled through the same seam POST uses before anything is written, so one graph gets one verdict from both verbs (Requirement 3.2) and an invalid one answers 422 with the full report having persisted nothing (Requirements 3.5, 3.6). The graph goes into `buy_logic` as the create path stores it, market identity comes from the DATA nodes (SB-06), and the compiled graph becomes a new current version - without which an edit kept the version its FIRST save produced and a backtest would have executed a plan the author had already replaced.

THE OWNERSHIP LIST WAS DEAD FOR EVERY USER. GET /api/library/my-strategies converted any exception on rounds 1 and 2 into MARKETPLACE_READ_FAILED, and their projections name columns only hand-applied migrations add: `strategies.is_active` (root 006), `strategies.archived_at` (005a), `library_subscriptions.period_expiry` and `renewal_enabled` (008). PostgREST errors the whole statement for one undefined column, so any single absent one rendered 'Ownership list unavailable' on every call. That is the incident `OWNED_STRATEGY_SELECT`'s docstring already records for `strategies.description`. The embed is a second instance: migration 006 gives `library_subscriptions` two foreign keys to `library_strategies`, which makes the unhinted `library_strategies!inner` ambiguous (PGRST201).

Both reads are now tiered. The narrow projection is attempted first and is what a correctly-migrated environment issues - same columns, same order, same one round trip - and a narrower one is tried only for an error `is_degradable_projection_error` recognises as 'that projection is unreadable'. A timeout, a refused connection, an RLS denial or a missing table still answers 503, so Requirements 1.5 and 1.7 are unweakened; the classifier is deliberately narrow for the reason `strategy_archive`'s equivalent is. `select('*')` is not the fallback: it would drag the Protected_Logic columns across the wire that the explicit list exists to keep off a list page.

Nothing is substituted for a value that was not read. A degraded round 1 omits the keys it did not request rather than nulling them, a degraded round 2 leaves `period_expiry` and `renewal_state` null - which `subscription_view` already defines as unavailable, never a default - and an exhausted round 2 reports `subscriptions_available: false` with the owned half still returned, the same disposition round 3 already takes for its count (Requirement 28.5). The page withholds the subscribed count instead of printing a measured-looking zero, and an empty list with the subscribed half unread is no longer the empty state, because that copy claims the account holds nothing. The failing column is now named in the logs, which is what an operator needs to decide whether to apply 006, 005a or 008.

Two baseline entries re-recorded with their `_baseline_note` justification: the three new keys on my_strategies' return, and the new DAG_INVALID_STATUS on update_strategy. Nothing removed or retyped.

Correct two false comments in the signup OTP path

Comments only - no behaviour changes, and deliberately so: the broken OTP flow is a Supabase project misconfiguration, not a code defect, and a frontend change cannot fix or detect it.

What was wrong. signUp's options carried 'The confirmation email carries a link as well as the 6-digit code', which is false for the stock Confirm-signup template: that template holds {{ .ConfirmationURL }} alone, so no code is ever printed and the OTP screen asks for something that was never sent. The line after it claimed to 'dispatch email verification OTP' when no dispatch happens at all - the only email is the one signUp already sent.

Both now state what actually occurs, and record the coupling that made this unfixable from the UI: the project's Email OTP Length must equal the six boxes this page renders and the /^\\d{6}$/ in handleVerifyOtp. It was set to 8, and an 8-digit code cannot be entered into six boxes, which left the confirmation link as the only way in and silently bypassed the password+OTP gate the invariant tests assert.

No shared OTP_LENGTH constant was introduced: the drift is server-side, so a frontend constant could not prevent a recurrence, and the length appears in aria-labels that auth_otp.test.jsx binds verbatim. ESLint 0 errors; 47 auth tests pass.

workflow_runs.display_title: Reject a demonstrably expired token in both auth guards

head_commit.message:
Reject a demonstrably expired token in both auth guards

AuthGuard and GuestGuard both branched on whether a token STRING existed, never on whether it was still valid. Two consequences, one reported and one worse.

Reported: a spent token left in sessionStorage made /signin and /signup permanently unreachable - GuestGuard bounced every visit straight to /app/dashboard, so a signed-out user could not get back to a sign-in form. Supabase persistSession restores a session into localStorage on boot and onAuthStateChange copies it into sessionStorage, so the stale value reappears on every load.

Worse: AuthGuard admitted an expired token to the app shell. The client gate did no validation, so the shell rendered and every read behind it answered 401 - a dashboard full of errors instead of a redirect to sign in.

getEffectiveToken now discards a token it can PROVE is past its own exp, and does not store an already-expired one arriving in the URL hash. Only a positively-provable expiry is rejected: a non-JWT, a malformed one, or a JWT with no exp claim is left exactly as before, so no existing caller or test that seeds an opaque token changes behaviour. The signature is deliberately not checked - the server holds the secret and rejects a forgery on every request; what only the client can notice is that the credential it is about to present is already dead.

Both guard bodies are unchanged, so the source-text contract in tests/unit/pages/authRedirectOrigin.test.jsx still holds. ESLint 0 errors; 537 passed across tests/unit/guards, tests/unit/pages, src/pages/__tests__ and auth_otp.

workflow_runs.display_title: Make the billing payment surface Razorpay-honest instead of dead Stripe

head_commit.message:
Make the billing payment surface Razorpay-honest instead of dead Stripe

The Payment methods panel was Stripe-shaped on a Razorpay platform and every one of its three couplings was dead: POST /portal opened with _validate_keys('stripe') so the panel's only button 500'd on every press; POST /payment-methods demanded brand/last4/expiry 'from the Stripe PaymentMethod response' and there is no Stripe.js anywhere in the frontend, so it always 422'd; GET /payment-methods reads the table only that write could fill, so it was always empty.

Worse than dead: the add path stored those four card attributes verbatim from the request body with nothing verifying them against any gateway, so a caller could mint a 'visa ****4242' no processor had seen and GET would present it to the account holder as their instrument. That write is deleted.

POST /portal is now provider-aware: 501 PROVIDER_HAS_NO_BILLING_PORTAL when a live provider simply has no hosted portal (Razorpay publishes none), 503 PAYMENT_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED when no provider holds live credentials - two different facts needing opposite fixes, so two codes. The Stripe branch is untouched and still runs when Stripe is genuinely configured. POST /payment-methods returns 501 PAYMENT_METHOD_STORAGE_UNSUPPORTED naming Razorpay tokenisation as the unimplemented piece; a malformed body still gets its own validation 422. DELETE keeps its real lookup and its true 404, now with a code and the reason the table is empty. No URL or card attribute is ever synthesised.

Frontend drops the dead Manage via provider portal button - no capability was behind it - and the empty state now states the truth: the instrument is collected by Razorpay Checkout at purchase and never held by VyomQuant. Stale Stripe docstrings corrected.

The validation sweep had been SKIPPING the portal route on its 500, so its never-500 assertion was never evaluated; it now genuinely exercises the route (381 passed/12 skipped -> 382/11). Three baselines re-recorded with evidence notes. New tests/test_billing_payment_surface_refusals.py (8 tests) drives the real mounted app.

workflow_runs.display_title: style(app): one visual language across every page

head_commit.message:
style(app): one visual language across every page

The landing page and the authenticated app already shared a token file. What
they did not share was a consistent application of it. This unifies the
application of the tokens without touching architecture, routing, data flow
or any feature.

THE BADGE WAS A DIFFERENT GREEN FROM THE WHOLE APP

components/ui/Badge.jsx held 68 raw colour literals, 40 of them #10B981 and
#EF4444 - the pre-convergence trading palette. tokens.css moved profit to
#26A69A and loss to #EF5350, and every components/ds/ status surface reads
those through design/semantic.js. So a ds/StrategyStatus reading RUNNING and
a ui/Badge reading RUNNING rendered two different greens in the same table,
on most pages in the product. This was the single most visible source of
"different theme per page".

Two of the 68 were not in the palette at all: #94A3B8 (draft) and #64748B
(stopped) are Tailwind's slate ramp with no token behind either; both
collapse onto content-secondary. The chip also now matches ds/StatusBadge in
shape - rounded-sm, text-micro, same mono/uppercase treatment - and its dot
no longer pulses, which ds/StatusBadge's "carries no pulse, no halo" test
names this component's dot as the thing it was written against.

no-colour-literals.budget.js had this entry annotated "task 6.6 is scheduled
to move ui/Badge.jsx's 40 #10B981/#EF4444 occurrences to the trading
palette. Out-of-scope does not mean unscheduled." This is that move. 68 -> 0.

BUTTONS LOOKED LIKE A DIFFERENT PRODUCT FROM THE INPUTS BESIDE THEM

ds/CommandButton wraps components/ui/Button.jsx, so it renders on every
authenticated page. It was deciding four things off-system:

  - 5 colour literals: text-[#080A0E] twice (which is content-inverse, and
    this budget's own notes already said so), hover:bg-[#33E0FF]
    (brand-hover), ring-offset-[#080A0E], and hover:bg-[#FCD34D] - an amber
    with no token behind it. 5 -> 0.
  - hover:border-cyan-500/50 on `secondary`: Tailwind's default cyan ramp,
    not the brand. It compiled and looked approximately right while being a
    different colour from every other hover in the product. Never a literal,
    so the guard never saw it.
  - font-mono on every label. App.jsx's shell comment states the rule this
    broke: mono is for "numeric cells, identifiers, timestamps and code
    only". Buttons are sans now.
  - rounded-lg, which is ds/Panel's CARD radius, while every ds/ control
    (ActionControl, Field, FilterBar, ErrorState's retry) is rounded-sm.

Sizes moved off raw text-xs/sm/base onto the declared steps. Padding is
unchanged, so no layout moves.

474 DEPRECATED TOKEN ALIASES RETIRED

tokens.css carries a compatibility block of ~20 deprecated names, each a
pure var() reference to a canonical token, kept alive so unmigrated surfaces
kept compiling. 474 occurrences across 11 files still read them -
accent-cyan, text-text-primary, bg-bg-elevated, border-border-default and so
on. All now read the canonical token. Because every alias is a pure
reference, the rendered colour is identical; what changes is that the
codebase states one name per colour, and the compat block moves closer to
deletion.

Notably NONE of the 21 src/pages/ files used them - the page migrations had
already finished. The stragglers were components/ui/*, the three builder
controls, admin, download, legal, waitlist, and landing/Pricing.jsx, which
was the one landing file the redesign left untouched.

RADIUS: NINE VALUES DOWN TO FOUR

ds/ uses lg for cards, md for floating surfaces, sm for controls, full for
dots. Outside it the tree also used rounded-xl (35 occurrences, only ever on
hand-rolled cards) and rounded-2xl, so a bespoke card at 12px sat beside a
ds/Panel at 8px. Both now resolve to rounded-lg. components/landing/ is
excluded: it deliberately runs a larger marketing scale.

ELEVATION THAT RAN BACKWARDS

bg-surface-canvas is the shell backdrop. Thirteen places used it as a FILL
on top of that same backdrop, so the card rendered darker than the surface
it sat on and only its border was visible - inverted elevation. Cards move
to surface-raised and wells to surface-inset, which is what tokens.css
declares each layer for. Page roots keep surface-canvas; that is its job.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED

The app's TYPE DENSITY. The landing page runs 16-18px body copy and 112px
section padding; the terminal runs 13px body and 10-11px labels because
DESIGN_SYSTEM_V2.md and the ui-redesign spec chose a dense scale for tables
of positions and orders. Applying marketing typography to a trading terminal
would put fewer rows on screen and make it worse, so the shared language
here is colour, radius, elevation and control treatment - not type size.

Also unchanged: every component's props and API, the shell geometry
constants (PAGE_HEADER 64, TOPBAR 56, SIDEBAR 216/56, all pinned inline so a
class cannot move them), and every data path.

A MISTAKE MADE AND REPAIRED IN THIS CHANGE

The radius pass was first applied with PowerShell Set-Content, which writes
the host's ANSI code page rather than UTF-8. It destroyed every non-ASCII
character in the two files it rewrote: PaperTrading.jsx came back with 269
U+FFFD replacement characters and Backtester.jsx with 144, breaking four
tests - the em dash in "Cash - available (USD)" and the ellipsis in "Choose
a strategy..." stopped matching their queries. Both files were restored from
HEAD and the pass re-applied through Node, which writes UTF-8 explicitly.

Separately, the bare `rounded` -> `rounded-sm` rule matched the ENGLISH WORD
"rounded" as readily as the class, corrupting 19 lines of prose across 12
files - docblocks explaining that figures are "never rounded", and three
user-visible strings: a capital-field hint reading "never a rounded float",
a paper-trading validation message, and two ds/Metric tooltips in
design/pageFields.js. All 19 are repaired; the files whose only change was
that substitution now have no diff at all, which is why they are absent from
this commit.

Verified: 1166 tests pass across the guards, landing, pages, ds and
page-test suites (56 files). Full suite 3645/3646, the one failure being a
file-walking test in canonicalGraph that passes in isolation and flakes under
parallel load - the module it checks for genuinely does not exist and has no
references, verified independently. Build clean, 0 lint errors, and a
whole-tree sweep confirms zero U+FFFD and zero prose occurrences remaining.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(css): layer the global reset, which was zeroing every spacing utiΓÇª

head_commit.message:
fix(css): layer the global reset, which was zeroing every spacing utility

THE DEFECT

src/index.css declared its global reset outside any cascade layer:

  * { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0; ... }

Cascade layers rank below unlayered CSS, always, whatever the
specificity. Tailwind v4 emits every utility into @layer utilities, so
that one rule at specificity (0,0,0) beat .py-20, .p-7, .mt-8, .mx-auto
and every other margin or padding utility in the bundle. Measured on the
production build: the reset compiled at byte offset 67210, outside all
five layers, while @layer utilities opened at 10567.

Symptoms, measured in Chromium at 1440x900 before the fix:

  - every <section> computed padding-top: 0 and padding-bottom: 0, so
    eleven sections butted against each other
  - .section-inner kept max-width: 80rem but computed margin-inline: 0px
    instead of auto, so every section pinned to the left viewport edge
  - the hero's pt-32 collapsed and the <h1> rendered underneath the
    fixed navbar
  - scrollbar-hide's scrollbar-width: none was overridden by the second
    unlayered `*` rule, so that utility was inert app-wide

Colour, border, max-width, display and gap were unaffected - none is a
margin or a padding - which is why it read as a badly designed page
rather than a broken stylesheet. gap surviving is the diagnostic detail:
grids kept their column gaps while the cards inside had no padding.

This reached every route, not just the landing page. It arrived in
cf6318c, which moved the reset out of the inline <style> AppShell
rendered - correct in itself, but as an inline <style> the reset was only
in the DOM while AppShell was mounted, i.e. /app/* only. Hoisting it into
index.css made it global and it began applying to the public routes.

After: sections compute 112px padding (py-28), hero 176px (pt-44),
content centres at 720 in a 1440 viewport, no overlaps, no horizontal
overflow. Verified at 1440x900 and 390x844.

A NEW GUARD, SO IT CANNOT COME BACK SILENTLY

tests/unit/guards/css-layer-order.test.js asserts that every
margin/padding reset in index.css sits inside a layer, pins the universal
and scrollbar resets by name, and asserts @utility blocks stay unlayered
(Tailwind assigns their layer, and demoting them would invert the
override they exist for). Source scan, no build needed.

Proven non-vacuous twice: a planted example, and by reintroducing the
real defect in index.css and confirming the guard fails on it.

SCROLL-MARGIN: THE OTHER NAVBAR COLLISION

Every Navbar and Footer link is an in-page scrollIntoView, which aligns
the section's top edge with the viewport top - and the navbar is fixed,
so each target section arrived with its eyebrow and heading hidden behind
it. section[id] now carries scroll-margin-top: 5.5rem. All five nav
anchors verified to land clear of the navbar.

DESIGN PASS

Colour. The page was one flat cyan: every icon, eyebrow and chip across
four sections, which is why they read as one undifferentiated wall. There
is now a four-hue stage language, repeated in the same order on
HowItWorks' steps and TrustSection's pillars so the two sections read as
one idea at two levels of detail:

  cyan   brand           build
  amber  status-warning  research
  indigo env-paper       paper - the app's own environment colour for
                         simulated execution, so the hue a visitor meets
                         on the landing page is the hue on their first
                         paper deployment
  teal   status-profit   live

Class strings are written out literally rather than composed: Tailwind v4
scans source as text, so an interpolated text-${hue} emits no CSS and the
icon silently inherits. A test asserts all four hues are present.

Typography. Monospace was carrying prose - eyebrows, card bodies,
captions, twelve feature chips - which read as log output rather than
marketing copy. Mono is now reserved for terminal chrome, technical
values (OHLCV feed, port type names) and ordinal counters: 45 uses down
to 20, and ProductTour alone from 16 to 6. Body copy moved off the 13px
app scale to 14-16px, section headings gained an lg step, and chips are
sans pills instead of mono boxes.

Surfaces. Cards sit on surface-raised rather than surface-panel so they
read as raised against the canvas instead of as outlines, with radius
lifted to match.

Hero. Three of the five pipeline stage labels wrapped to two lines in a
184px column and left the row visibly ragged; the labels are shorter and
the detail moved to the line beneath. The subhead lost a sentence.

No claim changed. Every removal from the previous commit still holds -
the invented performance figures, the withdrawn installer links, the
uncertified security badge, the 50+ exchanges claim - and the tests that
pin them are untouched.

Verified: 289 tests pass across the guards, landing, pricing and download
suites. Build clean, 0 lint errors.

head_commit.message:
feat(landing): rebuild the landing page around verifiable claims

Fourteen sections become twelve, and every claim on the page is now
traceable to a file in this repository.

REMOVED CLAIMS THAT WERE NOT TRUE
  ModernTradingSection advertised TWAP, VWAP and Iceberg order types and
  institutional FIX connectivity. None exists in backend_app/: the only
  VWAP is rolling_vwap in backend/indicators_backend.py, registered as an
  IndicatorSpec block rather than an execution algorithm. Section deleted;
  its one durable claim (direct CCXT.pro routing) moved to TrustSection.

  "50+ exchanges", in three places, against core/exchange_certification.py
  registering exactly one venue at LEVEL_5_PRODUCTION_READY. Now states the
  library's reach and the certified venue as separate sentences.

  "millions of backtest iterations in seconds" - nothing measures backtest
  throughput. Replaced with the Monte Carlo, walk-forward and sensitivity
  passes that optimization_engine.py really does run.

  The "Enterprise Security" badge, with no SOC 2, ISO 27001 or pen-test
  report behind it. The six controls were real; the badge implied an
  attestation. Now says plainly that no certification is held yet.

REMOVED INVENTED PERFORMANCE FIGURES
  Hero carried Sharpe 2.1, Win Rate 67.4%, Max DD -8.2%; the tour carried
  +28.4% net return, Sharpe 2.14, Sortino 3.08, Profit Factor 1.82 and a
  monotonically rising equity curve. None came from a backtest, and the
  footer on the same page states VyomQuant is not a registered investment
  adviser. A test now asserts all nine figures and five metric labels stay
  off the page.

FIXED ELEVEN DEAD ENDS
  Hero, Navbar, FinalCTA and Footer advertised Windows and macOS installers
  pointing into /download#windows and #macos, where every artifact renders
  unavailable - while DownloadSection said on the same page that the builds
  are not published. Three of the hero's six CTAs led nowhere.

  DownloadSection is KEPT and reframed: the Tauri desktop builds are real
  and shipping, so the section announces them as in final testing while
  each of the four PlatformArtifact panels still reports its own true
  state. Footer's #features anchor, inert for the life of the file, now
  points at #platform.

  Footer's social links were fetched. github.com/VyomQuant and
  linkedin.com/company/vyomquant both 404; the Discord vanity invite cannot
  be verified server-side. All three removed, commented in place for
  one-line restoration. Only the X account, which resolves, remains.

ADDED WHAT WAS MISSING
  ProofStrip - the credibility band under the hero. Six items, each naming
  a mechanism in the backend, because no customer count, testimonial,
  certification or funding claim exists to borrow credibility from.

  MarketplaceSection - /marketplace is a public route the old page linked
  to zero times. Framed as browse, clone and publish only: the spec audit
  classifies marketplace checkout and the 90/10 split as broken and the
  payout ledger as missing, so no revenue share is promised.

MERGED AND RENAMED
  TrustSection, ScreenshotsSection, ModernTradingSection and HowItWorks
  pitched the same four capabilities - twenty feature cards for four
  features. TrustSection now states each pillar once; ProductTour shows
  each in use. Waitlist deleted (it competed with a working signup);
  FounderSection deleted (a bio mid-funnel).

  ScreenshotsSection.jsx -> ProductTour.jsx. The page carries no product
  screenshots and has settled on carrying none, so the old name promised
  something deliberately absent.

Pricing.jsx is untouched: the four INR tiers are a published commitment
matching core/subscription_engine.py.

RATCHETS TIGHTENED, NOT LOOSENED
  absolute-font-sizes: all four landing entries deleted at zero (16
    text-[Npx] became declared token steps).
  no-colour-literals: Hero and the tour lowered 3 -> 0; six hand-mixed
    hex backgrounds and rgba glows became token utilities.
  dead-tailwind: KNOWN_DEAD_CLASSES is now empty. animate-pulse-glow went
    with the rewritten CTA button.
  a11y-ratchet: list tracks the new section set, no waivers - zero
    accessibility findings. ProductTour also gained a real ARIA tab widget;
    the previous one had role="tab" with no tablist, no aria-controls and
    no keyboard handling.

Verified: 448 tests pass across the guards, landing and pages suites.
Production build clean, landing chunk 54.8 kB / 14.9 kB gzip, 0 lint
errors. Pre-existing failures in dashboard_phase2a_ui,
dashboard_phase2d_polish and ds/Chart are unrelated and were confirmed to
fail identically with this change set fully reverted.
